articles.originalTitle: On World Architecture Day 2026: A Call to Build Better, Build Differently, and Share Resources - archdaily.com
articles.title: International Union of Architects Highlights Global Housing Crisis on World Architecture Day
articles.excerpt: The International Union of Architects marked World Architecture Day by drawing attention to the global housing crisis and equitable access to housing.
articles.content: The International Union of Architects designates the first Monday of October as World Architecture Day, aligning with the United Nations' World Habitat Day. Both occasions drew attention to the global housing crisis as a fundamental element of human dignity and well-being. The union's motto, "Housing is a Human Right. Build It," calls on architects to advance equitable access to housing through design, research, and advocacy. According to United Nations figures, more than 3 billion people lack adequate housing, over 1.1 billion live in informal settlements, and hundreds of millions experience homelessness. The International Union of Architects is a global non-governmental federation uniting professional organizations from more than 120 countries and territories. Recognizing housing shortages as a pressing challenge, the federation emphasizes that housing must not be treated as a luxury asset. On World Architecture Day, the organization invited architects worldwide to promote creative strategies through lectures, exhibitions, and public outreach to address these systemic issues.

articles.originalTitle: Art Basel announces 272 exhibitors and a reconfigured showfloor for its 2026 Miami Beach edition - Art Basel
articles.title: Art Basel Miami Beach 2026 Announces 272 Exhibitors
articles.excerpt: Art Basel Miami Beach has announced its 2026 exhibitor line-up featuring 272 participants from over 40 countries alongside a reconfigured floor plan. The event will take place from December 4 to 6 at the Miami Beach Convention Center.
articles.content: Art Basel Miami Beach will bring together 272 exhibitors from more than 40 countries and territories for its upcoming edition. Scheduled for December 4 through 6 at the Miami Beach Convention Center, the fair will host VIP preview days on December 2 and 3. Organizers introduced a substantially reconfigured floor plan based on feedback from the selection committee and exhibitors. The new layout occupies approximately 12 percent less floor space, while the main Galleries sector features roughly 10 percent fewer exhibitors to create a more concentrated setting. Organized around four hospitality plazas rather than five, the redesigned floor plan opens longer sightlines across the convention center. The fair comprises four distinct sectors, including Galleries with 204 exhibitors, alongside Kabinett, Nova, Positions, and Survey. Latin America and the Caribbean maintain a robust presence, with Brazil representing the third-largest national contingent. More than thirty galleries will participate in the Miami Beach edition for the first time, predominantly through project-based sectors. Public art installations, digital presentations through Zero 10, and external sculptural projects will accompany the main exhibition halls during the December event.

articles.originalTitle: Painting large as an Impressionist: Renoir and the full-length format | Events - The National Gallery, London
articles.title: National Gallery Examines Renoir and Full-Length Portraiture
articles.excerpt: Colin B. Bailey, Director of The Morgan Library and Museum, will deliver a special lecture at the National Gallery's Pigott Theatre exploring Pierre-Auguste Renoir's large-scale portraits.
articles.content: The National Gallery is hosting a special event focusing on Pierre-Auguste Renoir's full-length portraits, recognized among the most ambitious works of his career. Held in conjunction with the exhibition Renoir and Love, the lecture features Colin B. Bailey, Katharine J. Rayner Director of The Morgan Library & Museum, who will examine how the artist captured modern life, emotions, and social interactions in 19th-century Paris. Drawing on decades of research into eighteenth- and nineteenth-century French art, Bailey will explore Renoir's technical brilliance, evolving portraiture approach, and psychological immediacy. The talk will take place in the Pigott Theatre on Level -1 of the Sainsbury Wing. Standard tickets are priced at 10 pounds, while concessions are available at 8 pounds for full-time students, jobseekers, and disabled adults. Advance booking is required for attendance, and members will have the option to join the event online. This lecture offers audiences a distinct opportunity to closely examine the artist's celebrated figures within the broader context of friendship, love, and modernity explored throughout the exhibition.

articles.originalTitle: Renoir and Love | Exhibitions - The National Gallery, London
articles.title: National Gallery in London Opens Major Renoir and Love Exhibition
articles.excerpt: The National Gallery in London presents Renoir and Love, an exhibition exploring the artist's depiction of human connections and everyday emotions through 40 paintings gathered from international collections, on view until January 31, 2027.
articles.content: The National Gallery in London presents Renoir and Love, an exhibition focusing on Pierre-Auguste Renoir's exploration of love, friendship, and human connection during his peak period from the 1860s to the 1880s. Running until January 31, 2027, the exhibition brings together 40 paintings from collections across the world, highlighting the artist's role as an innovator of Impressionism. Notably, Renoir's iconic 1876 painting Bal au Moulin de la Galette from the Musée d'Orsay is on display in the United Kingdom for the first time. The exhibition is organized jointly by the Musée d'Orsay, the National Gallery, and the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston. Visitors can explore sun-dappled gardens, dance halls, and intimate everyday moments captured by the artist, with flexible pay-what-you-wish admission options available on select Friday evenings.

articles.originalTitle: Laila Majid and Louis Blue Newby’s Feed Logic - ArtReview
articles.title: London Exhibition Examines the Evolving Nature of Visual Culture
articles.excerpt: Laila Majid and Louis Blue Newby's Bizarre Life exhibition questions the iconographic power of images that lose their photographic identity in the digital age. The show runs until October 3 at Niru Ratnam in London.
articles.content: Artists Laila Majid and Louis Blue Newby explore the logic of the digital feed through drawings, collages, and video works in their exhibition Bizarre Life at Niru Ratnam gallery. The graphite drawings in the Contact series utilize thermal printing software and redrawn lines to present blurred figures, examining the decontextualization of random internet imagery. Wall-mounted assemblages in the Spread series place photographic prints beneath leather-textured silicone skins, juxtaposing everyday objects with unfamiliar elements. The vertical video works, including Inner Heat, bring visual instability into motion through low-resolution, reversed footage of fireworks and a slowed concert recording of Taylor Swift where stage lighting and camera variables abstract the singer's body. Through these distinct visual experiments, the works suggest that images can surrender their photographic identities while retaining a distinct iconographic power. The exhibition remains deliberately unresolved regarding whether this phenomenon serves as a connective or unsettling force for contemporary viewers.

articles.originalTitle: Exhibition at New York's Met examines how Lee Krasner and Jackson Pollock's relationship enriched their art - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art Examines Lee Krasner and Jackson Pollock Relationship
articles.excerpt: A new exhibition at the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York examines the artistic and personal relationship of Abstract Expressionist figures Lee Krasner and Jackson Pollock through over 120 works.
articles.content: The Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York is presenting Krasner and Pollock: Past Continuous, an exhibition exploring the personal and professional relationship between artists Lee Krasner and Jackson Pollock. Curated by David Breslin and Brinda Kumar, the exhibition spans more than 120 paintings, works on paper, and ephemera sourced partly from private collections. As the museum's first major exhibition dedicated to either artist, the presentation displays their full careers side-by-side rather than focusing solely on their time together on Long Island. The curators note that the exhibition provides Krasner's work an opportunity to emerge from Pollock's shadow while highlighting her labor in stewarding his posthumous market after his death. The chronological display illustrates collage as a central metaphor for their creative dialogue, presenting them as each other's primary critics. The exhibition runs from October 4 through January 31, 2027.

articles.originalTitle: The 90s: Art and Fashion - tate.org.uk
articles.title: Tate Britain Explores the Intersection of Art and Fashion in the 1990s
articles.excerpt: Tate Britain presents The 90s: Art and Fashion, an exhibition exploring the creative energy and cultural shifts of the 1990s through photography, fashion, art, and design.
articles.content: Tate Britain presents The 90s: Art and Fashion, an exhibition drawing on the experiences of curator Edward Enninful OBE to examine a decade marked by bold creativity and cultural transformation. Bringing together photography, fashion, art, and design, the exhibition highlights a period when a new generation reshaped British culture by breaking down traditional boundaries between disciplines. Visitors can encounter iconic works by artists and photographers including Steve McQueen, Sarah Lucas, Yinka Shonibare, Corinne Day, and Juergen Teller, alongside fashion creations by Vivienne Westwood, Alexander McQueen, and John Galliano. Featured works include Mark Leckey's video compilation tracing British dance music culture, a tartan look from Vivienne Westwood's Anglomania collection reflecting historical fashion references, and Yinka Shonibare's reconfiguration of The Swing connecting colonial histories to European art. The display also features Steve McQueen's silent film Bear, Abigail Lane's intimate wallpaper installation, and Jim Lambie's psychedelic floor design created from industrial vinyl tape. The exhibition runs from October 8, 2026, to February 14, 2027, with free admission for members. An audio guide featuring insights from curators and artists is available for an additional purchase.

articles.originalTitle: Roy Lichtenstein: Like New | Museum Exhibitions | News - Gagosian
articles.title: Roy Lichtenstein Retrospective Opens at Whitney Museum in New York
articles.excerpt: The Whitney Museum of American Art presents Roy Lichtenstein: Like New, marking the artist's first retrospective in New York since 1993 and gathering roughly 130 works created from the early 1940s through the 1990s.
articles.content: The Whitney Museum of American Art in New York hosts Roy Lichtenstein: Like New from October 11, 2026, to May 10, 2027. Marking the artist's first major retrospective in the city since 1993, the exhibition traces how Lichtenstein's early interest in perception and visual recognition shaped a career-long investigation into duplication, simulation, and image culture. Featuring approximately 130 works produced from the early 1940s to the 1990s, the exhibition explores his treatment of images as unstable forms subject to borrowing, translation, and reframing. For the first time, all works from Lichtenstein's inaugural Pop-style exhibition at the Leo Castelli Gallery in 1962 are reunited. This pivotal moment defined an era and extended its impact beyond Pop art, shaping subsequent generations of artists whose works are also displayed within the exhibition.

articles.originalTitle: Contemporary Istanbul founder planning new fair on city's Asian side - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Contemporary Istanbul Founder Planning New Fair on City's Asian Side
articles.excerpt: Following Contemporary Istanbul at Tersane Istanbul, founder Ali Güreli plans to launch a new fair on the city's Asian side and discusses pursuing an art tax reform similar to Italy's.
articles.content: Türkiye's largest contemporary art fair, Contemporary Istanbul, took place for the third consecutive year at Tersane Istanbul along the Golden Horn with around 70 exhibitors from over 15 countries. Fair founder and chairman of the board Ali Güreli announced plans to launch another fair on the city's Asian side, alongside returning in 2027 during the same week as the 19th Istanbul Biennial. Güreli also added that discussions are underway with the Ministry of Culture and Tourism regarding an art taxation reform similar to Italy's 5% cutdown on art acquisitions. This edition featured international debuts such as Jessica Silverman Gallery and Galeria Karla Osorio, alongside Asian participants including Pearl Lam Projects, Whitestone Gallery, and Silk Art House Gallery. The event additionally hosted emerging technological platforms such as Numeraire Future Trends, providing AI-run authentication and valuation demonstrations for collectors. Local galleries and participants noted that the venue layout facilitated a successful flow and robust engagement during the opening days.

articles.originalTitle: Patek Philippe Unveils Seventh Watch Art Grand Exhibition in Milan, Debuts Limited-edition Timepieces - WWD
articles.title: Patek Philippe Launches Watch Art Grand Exhibition in Milan
articles.excerpt: Patek Philippe has launched its largest Watch Art Grand Exhibition to date at CityOval Milano, debuting seven new limited-edition timepieces alongside historical collections.
articles.content: Swiss watchmaker Patek Philippe has opened its seventh Watch Art Grand Exhibition in Milan. Spanning 31,215 square feet at the recently renovated CityOval Milano venue, the exhibition displays over 500 timepieces, including the 1868 wristwatch owned by Countess Koscowicz of Hungary. Company president Thierry Stern noted the longstanding importance of the Italian market and its connoisseurs of rare handcrafts. Running through Oct. 18, the exhibition follows previous editions in cities such as Munich, London, New York, Singapore, Tokyo, and Dubai. To mark the Milan edition, Patek Philippe debuted seven new limited-edition timepieces featuring sapphire crystal casebacks inscribed with 'Patek Philippe Milano 2026.' These include three Calatrava iterations with red, white, and green lacquered dials representing the Italian flag, alongside world time minute repeaters featuring enameled maps of downtown Milan. The brand also introduced the Gondolo Ladies First collection of cushion-shaped jewelry watches featuring gem-set dials and quartz movements. The exhibition coincides with Milano Watch Week at Palazzo Mezzanotte, highlighting the city's growing status as a high-watchmaking hub.

articles.originalTitle: Patek Philippe Unveils Seventh Watch Art Grand Exhibition in Milan, Debuts Limited-edition Timepieces - wwd.com
articles.title: Patek Philippe Stages Seventh Watch Art Grand Exhibition in Milan
articles.excerpt: Patek Philippe has launched its largest Watch Art Grand Exhibition to date at CityOval Milano, featuring over 500 timepieces and several market-exclusive limited editions.
articles.content: Swiss watchmaker Patek Philippe opened its seventh and largest Watch Art Grand Exhibition at CityOval Milano, a recently renovated Art Nouveau venue formerly known as Palazzo delle Scintille. Spanning 31,215 square feet, the exhibition displays over 500 timepieces, including the brand's 1868 wristwatch created for Countess Koscowicz of Hungary. Speaking at the preview, president Thierry Stern highlighted Italy as a market of long-standing importance for rare handcrafts and technical excellence. The exhibition features 25 exclusive pieces inspired by the Italian landscape and culture, such as a dome table clock depicting Sicilian oranges and an Ellipse wristwatch portraying a Tuscan sunset. Marking the occasion, Patek Philippe debuted seven new limited-edition references featuring sapphire crystal casebacks inscribed with Patek Philippe Milano 2026. These include three Calatrava models with lacquered dials in green, white, and red, alongside world time minute-repeaters featuring maps of downtown Milan. The brand also introduced the Gondolo Ladies First jewelry collection. The exhibition runs through Oct. 18.

articles.originalTitle: Pattani Biennale 2026 Review: A Hopeful Aftertaste - ArtReview
articles.title: Pattani Biennale 2026 Connects Local Struggles and Art in Southern Thailand
articles.excerpt: The Pattani Biennale 2026 in Thailand explores regional social movements, community-led environmental projects, and identity struggles through contemporary art.
articles.content: The Pattani Biennale 2026, taking place across various venues in Pattani, Thailand, engages with the region's complex social fabric, insurgency background, and community struggles through contemporary art. The exhibition features contributions from the Deep South alongside artists from Malaysia, Indonesia, Laos, Myanmar, and other regions, utilizing local venues such as a juvenile home, university dormitories, and riverbanks. Artists Iris Sham and Louisa Mammeri presented a performance invoking a local proverb, merging food tasting with discussions on politics and biochemistry across different regions. Other works address local environmental and economic shifts, including Pichai Pongsasaovapark’s installation referencing the decommissioning of 48 wooden fishing trawlers as part of a government vessel buyout policy, alongside commentary on warming sea temperatures. A university display highlights a women's collective striving to protect their coastal village from a proposed gas pipeline project, while young LGBTQ+ individuals contributed clay sculptures under guidance. The exhibition remains on view across Pattani through November 1.

articles.originalTitle: New Work: The Long Goodbye by Carrie Mae Weems - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Carrie Mae Weems's New Work Premieres at V&A East Museum
articles.excerpt: Artist Carrie Mae Weems's film The Long Goodbye, commissioned for the V&A East Museum, explores migration and the obscured love stories intertwined within these journeys.
articles.content: Artist Carrie Mae Weems's work The Long Goodbye, developed over nearly 3 years, has been presented for the opening of the V&A East Museum. Commissioned for the institution, the film explores migration through the love stories intertwined within these journeys. The project aims to restore humanity to individuals whose lives are frequently reduced to statistics. Informed by debates surrounding migration in Britain and the United States, the film examines how images and archives define established historical narratives. Using water and the ocean as central motifs representing migration routes, the work also invokes the concept of tidalectics. Shown at the V&A East Museum alongside two archival films by the artist, Before the Loss of You and Okwui, the project invites viewers to question inherited histories and recognize humanity across time and place.

articles.originalTitle: A Metal-Clad Mass-Timber Building by Lever Architecture Unites Portland State University’s Art and Design School - Architectural Record
articles.title: Portland State University Opens New Art and Design Building
articles.excerpt: Designed by Lever Architecture, the four-story Jordan Schnitzer School of Art + Art History + Design unites three major university departments under one roof.
articles.content: Opening on the campus of Portland State University, the nearly 107,000-square-foot building unites three major departments previously dispersed across campus under a single roof for the first time. Designed by Lever Architecture, the four-story structure is wrapped in forest canopy-evoking green metal panels, utilizing cross-laminated timber floor panels and a glulam column-and-beam system. More than half of the Douglas fir glulam used in the construction was sourced by Portland-based fabricator Timberlab from tribally owned forests across the Pacific Northwest. The building marks Portland State University's first mass-timber structure and the first ground-up university building designed by Lever. The design is composed of three distinct frames pinwheeling around a central commons space, which provides direct access to an open-air courtyard for student use. Upper levels contain classrooms, studios, labs, faculty offices, and a rooftop patio with planter beds. Completed in July 2026, the construction cost of the project reached $74 million. Structural engineering for the project was provided by KPFF, and Swinerton served as the general contractor.

articles.originalTitle: White-brick extension defines Design Museum Gent revamp - Dezeen
articles.title: Design Museum Gent Revamped with Waste-Based White Brick Extension
articles.excerpt: Architecture studios Carmody Groarke, Atama and Re-st have completed the comprehensive revamp of Design Museum Gent in Belgium.
articles.content: Architecture studios Carmody Groarke, Atama and Re-st have completed the revamp of Design Museum Gent in Belgium, adding a geometric volume wrapped in waste-based white bricks. The timber-framed wing introduces educational and event spaces to the museum, along with additional exhibition space. The team has restored the museum's three historic wings and renovated an existing courtyard. Described as the final piece of the museum site, the extension was designed to unite the collection and complete the visitor loop. The 2,200-square-metre expansion makes the building Belgium's largest design museum, spanning a total of 8,600 square metres. For the extension's design, the studios referenced Ghent's traditional gabled houses, resulting in a sloping profile and the use of limestone bricks. Produced using local construction waste and a low-energy lime-curing process in collaboration with Local Works Studio and BC Materials, the bricks are claimed to carry just one-third of the embodied carbon of a typical Belgian clay brick. The six-storey extension opens to a reception and shop at ground level, with education spaces across middle floors and an event space crowning the building. The museum reopens to the public on October 3 with a new art collection.

articles.originalTitle: A Warehouse is Converted Into the New Home for Architecture at MIT - Architectural Record
articles.title: MIT Architecture Department Relocates to Historic Converted Warehouse
articles.excerpt: Designed by Diller Scofidio + Renfro with Leers Weinzapfel, a converted 195,000-square-foot warehouse now houses the MIT Department of Architecture.
articles.content: The Massachusetts Institute of Technology architecture department relocated in August to a 195,000-square-foot converted warehouse located across the street. Designed by Diller Scofidio + Renfro in collaboration with Leers Weinzapfel, the conversion project repurposes the five-story brick structure, parts of which date back to 1894, into a new home for architecture, urban studies and planning, and the Morningside Academy for Design. To accommodate these programs within the existing masonry structure featuring low ceilings and a cell-like plan, the design team cut multistory voids within each block and inserted lightweight structural elements to create column-free studio spaces. The conversion incorporates newly cut gridded windows, full-height curtain walls, and concrete shear walls added at the building corners for structural support. Known as the Met Warehouse, the facility also hosts entrepreneurship programs linking the school with surrounding technology and bioscience enterprises.

articles.originalTitle: In Oregon, an Elegant Mass-Timber Library by Holst Architecture Makes a Grand Civic Statement - architecturalrecord.com
articles.title: New Mass-Timber Library Designed by Holst Architecture Opens in Oregon
articles.excerpt: The new 95,000-square-foot East County Library in Gresham, Oregon, provides a prominent civic addition designed by Holst Architecture.
articles.content: The East County Library in Gresham, Oregon, has been designed by Holst Architecture to address regional community needs. Spanning 95,000 square feet and costing $163 million, the facility matches the size of the library system's largest existing branch in downtown Portland. Rising on a former light-rail park-and-ride site, the two-story building stands 59 feet high. Community outreach played a central role during the planning process, resulting in programmatic additions such as a large auditorium available for free community reservation, calm rooms for neurodivergent users, and a recording studio. Holst Architecture worked alongside Adjaye Associates during early development before completing the project. The mass-timber structure features 96 columns, 1,200 beams, and 300 cross-laminated timber panels developed in collaboration with Timberlab. The project reached completion in May 2026.

articles.originalTitle: A Warehouse is Converted Into the New Home for Architecture at MIT - architecturalrecord.com
articles.title: MIT Architecture Department Moves Into Converted 19th-Century Warehouse in Cambridge
articles.excerpt: MIT's architecture department has relocated to a 195000-square-foot converted historic warehouse in Cambridge, designed by Diller Scofidio + Renfro alongside Leers Weinzapfel.
articles.content: After occupying residual spaces for much of its history, MIT's architecture department relocated in August to a 195000-square-foot converted warehouse across the street. Designed by Diller Scofidio + Renfro with Leers Weinzapfel, the project involved transforming the 500-foot-long, five-story brick structure, which dates back to 1894. The building previously served as the Metropolitan Storage Warehouse before being acquired by MIT in 1962 and operating as a warehouse until 2015. To accommodate the architecture department, the department of urban studies and planning, and the Morningside Academy for Design, the architects utilized a subtraction design strategy. This involved cutting multistory voids within the five warehouse blocks and inserting lightweight structures hanging from the roof to create column-free studio areas. The intervention includes contemporary glass additions, north-facing curtain walls, and a multilevel circulation spine, paired with necessary structural sutures and supports such as concrete shear walls added by the Cambridge Historical Commission guidelines.

articles.originalTitle: São Paulo’s Museu de Arte Moderna reopens after two-year renovation - theartnewspaper.com
articles.title: São Paulo's Museu de Arte Moderna Reopens After Two-Year Renovation
articles.excerpt: Reopening its doors following a two-year closure, the Museu de Arte Moderna de São Paulo resumed operations not with its permanent collection, but with the 39th Panorama of Brazilian Art curated by Diane Lima.
articles.content: Reopening its doors after a two-year renovation period, the Museu de Arte Moderna de São Paulo marked its return not with a permanent collection display, but with the 39th Panorama of Brazilian Art titled After It's All Said, running until 24 January 2027 at the Oscar Niemeyer-designed pavilion in Ibirapuera Park. The exhibition is curated by Diane Lima. Chief curator Cauê Alves noted that during the museum's two-year physical closure, the institution was active, holding more than a dozen exhibitions in other venues. Curator Diane Lima stated that the exhibition's title draws from the anti-colonial, Black feminist perspective of philosopher and visual artist Denise Ferreira da Silva. Lima explained that the presentation questions how artistic practices expand the limits of representation through radical imagination. The current edition features 33 artists, none of whom have participated in prior iterations. The participants experiment with form, materiality, and representation.

articles.originalTitle: Open call: Commissions for English Ceramic Circle Centenary display at V&A South Kensington - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: V&A and English Ceramic Circle Launch Open Call for Centenary Display
articles.excerpt: The English Ceramic Circle has announced plans to commission up to new works for a centenary display at V&A South Kensington, with submissions closing on November 15, 2026.
articles.content: The English Ceramic Circle, the largest and oldest society dedicated to the study of British ceramics and enamels, is marking its 100th anniversary with a special display at V&A South Kensington. Running from October 2027 to September 2028, the exhibition will highlight artistic and technological contributions from potters working in Britain from 1600 to the present. To support this display, the circle is seeking to commission up to three new works through an open submission process aimed at UK-based ceramic artists. Organizers particularly encourage proposals from early- and mid-career practitioners with between 3 and 15 years of experience working with clay. Selected artists will receive a fee of 3,000 pounds per artist and will work alongside curatorial staff to develop their projects. Finished works must be delivered to the museum by September 2027 for exhibition in Room 146. Applications require a 300-word artist statement and a 500-word proposal detailing the idea, physical form, dimensions, and materials. The deadline for submissions is November 15, 2026, with successful applicants notified in December 2026. The acquired works will ultimately be donated to a public museum in the UK following the conclusion of the display.

articles.originalTitle: TfL reveals civil engineering behind £15.3M step-free upgrades at Surrey Quays and Northolt - New Civil Engineer
articles.title: Step-Free Access Projects Completed at Surrey Quays and Northolt London Stations
articles.excerpt: Transport for London has completed step-free access improvements at Surrey Quays and Northolt stations, enhancing journeys for wheelchair users and passengers with luggage.
articles.content: Surrey Quays and Northolt stations in London have received new step-free access facilities, improving journeys for wheelchair users, parents with pushchairs, and passengers with luggage. According to Transport for London, the upgrades at Surrey Quays feature a new ticket hall, footbridge, lifts, and accessible toilet facilities, funded in part by the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government through its Housing Infrastructure Fund. Designer AtkinsRéalis and contractor Morgan Sindall Infrastructure focused on low-carbon materials, including low-carbon concrete and electric arc furnace steel, to minimize the carbon impact of the development. Meanwhile, Northolt station on the Central line received a new footbridge and lift, becoming the 95th station on the Tube network to offer step-free access. The Northolt project cost an estimated £15.3 million. Both station enhancements aim to increase capacity, reduce congestion, and improve travel options across the network.

articles.originalTitle: Basquiat, the Blue Ribbon Paintings, and the Art of Reproduction | Museum Exhibitions | News - Gagosian
articles.title: Princeton University Art Museum Exhibits Jean-Michel Basquiat’s Blue Ribbon Paintings
articles.excerpt: The Princeton University Art Museum has announced an exhibition examining Jean-Michel Basquiat's radical engagement with reproductive media, bringing together eleven Blue Ribbon paintings from 1984 alongside his known print projects.
articles.content: The Princeton University Art Museum in New Jersey is organizing an exhibition exploring Jean-Michel Basquiat's radical engagement with reproductive media from October 4, 2026, to January 31, 2027. At the center of the exhibition are the artist's Blue Ribbon paintings, eleven lesser-known works from 1984 featuring densely layered imagery such as anatomical diagrams, film logos, and crowned figures. The show examines Basquiat's connections with other artists and pioneering Black printmakers, revealing a lineage of Black experimentation and intergenerational exchange within reproductive media. By assembling nearly all of the artist's known print projects, the exhibition frames Basquiat as a conceptual artist probing identity, reproduction, and visibility within an increasingly commercialized art world. The broader cultural context also features developments such as Adriana Varejão's preparations to represent Brazil at the 61st Biennale di Venezia and ongoing artistic initiatives curated by figures like Wang Shu and Lu Wenyu for upcoming international exhibitions.

articles.originalTitle: Black Wall Street Journey: Re and De Imagining Black Progress: Rick Lowe | Museum Exhibitions | News - Gagosian
articles.title: Rick Lowe Exhibition Opens at University of Michigan Museum of Art
articles.excerpt: Black Wall Street Journey, Rick Lowe's largest institutional solo exhibition in the United States, has opened at the University of Michigan Museum of Art in Ann Arbor through January 24, 2027.
articles.content: Rick Lowe's public art project Black Wall Street Journey has opened at the University of Michigan Museum of Art as the artist's largest institutional solo exhibition in the United States. On view in Ann Arbor through January 24, 2027, the exhibition brings together painting, sculpture, and public installation to examine how Black prosperity, resilience, and self-determination are represented, measured, and understood. The presentation reflects the culmination of the artist's three-year residency at the institution and mirrors his deep engagement with researchers, data scientists, and numerous students. Working collaboratively across art, data, and inquiry, Lowe examines the forces that shape Black wealth and opportunity, ranging from income and education to housing and business ownership.

articles.originalTitle: Advancement in Shallow Foundations - American Society of Civil Engineers (ASCE)
articles.title: Geo-Institute to Host Session on Shallow Foundations and Ground Improvement
articles.excerpt: The Geo-Institute Shallow Foundations Technical Committee will host a live web conference addressing ground improvement technologies, subgrade reaction modulus, and recycled plastic pins.
articles.content: The Geo-Institute Shallow Foundations Technical Committee is scheduled to stream a technical session focusing on advanced shallow foundation practices and ground improvement methods. Presentations will examine shallow foundations with ground improvement in North Texas, redevelopment challenges at the National Western Center in Denver, the modulus of subgrade reaction, and the stabilization of airfield pavement subgrades using recycled plastic pins. Presenters will discuss how techniques such as lightweight cellular concrete can stabilize sites containing uncontrolled fill materials, including coal ash and organic debris, while generating substantial cost savings. The sessions also analyze the fundamental concepts governing the modulus of subgrade reaction, utilizing comprehensive databases from plate load tests and large mat foundation case histories to evaluate scale effects. Furthermore, the event will review the effectiveness of recycled plastic pins in controlling soil deformation under rapid airfield matting systems.

articles.originalTitle: Chanel Brings Le19M Closer to Chinese Art World, Local Craft With Pudong Art Exhibition - WWD
articles.title: Chanel Unveils La Galerie Du 19M Exhibition in Shanghai
articles.excerpt: Chanel has launched the largest iteration of its La Galerie Du 19M project at the Museum of Art Pudong in Shanghai, uniting French craftsmanship with Chinese artists.
articles.content: French luxury fashion house Chanel has launched the latest edition of its La Galerie Du 19M project at the Museum of Art Pudong in Shanghai. Titled 'A Sense Of Touch,' the exhibition occupies the entire third floor and marks the brand's largest local project to date following previous iterations in Dakar and Tokyo. The project showcases the history and craftsmanship of Chanel's Métiers d'Art hub, featuring collaborations with over 31 creative guests from China and France. Bruno Pavlovsky, president of fashion at Chanel SAS, noted that the exhibition highlights the intangible creative processes behind the brand. Curated by an editorial committee comprising Gong Yan, Lin Tianmiao, Zhang Lei, and Christelle Kocher, the display emphasizes sustainability through the transformation of discarded and leftover materials into works of art. Chinese artists such as Yin Xiuzhen, Ding Yi, and Lin Tianmiao contributed pieces created in collaboration with workshops like Lesage and Massaro. Running until Nov. 15, the exhibition includes public talks and interactive workshops for visitors.
